requirement: Extract the outbound links of a scraped HTML page with lxml, resolved to absolute URLs, without fragments, duplicates, non-web schemes or nofollow links.
skeleton: An allowed scheme set, a PageError, and extract_links parsing with document_fromstring, resolving links against base href, filtering by rel and scheme, stripping fragments and deduplicating in order.
caption: Collecting outbound links from an HTML page with lxml.html and urllib.parse. PageError is a plain Exception. extract_links(document, base_url) raises PageError for a blank document or when document_fromstring does not return an HtmlElement, then calls make_links_absolute with resolve_base_href=True so a base element wins over the page URL. It walks every a element, skips a missing href and any link whose rel tokens include nofollow compared case-insensitively, strips the fragment with urldefrag, keeps only http and https schemes checked with urlsplit, and returns each URL once in first-seen order. The fixture asserts relative links resolve, base href overrides the page URL, fragments and duplicates collapse, mailto, javascript, ftp and tel links are skipped, nofollow and href-less anchors are dropped, and a blank page raises PageError.

plan.intent: Build the frontier for a polite web crawler
constraints: Links resolve against a base element when present
Fragments are stripped and each URL appears once
Only http and https links are returned
Links with a nofollow rel token, in any case, are skipped

rationale.teaches: Let lxml resolve links with make_links_absolute(resolve_base_href=True), then normalise with urldefrag and filter schemes with urlsplit.
rationale.why: Ignoring base href crawls the wrong host, keeping fragments or duplicates multiplies work, and mailto or javascript URLs break the fetcher.

ops.docstring: Collect absolute, deduplicated outbound links from an HTML page with lxml.

ops.source:
class PageError(Exception):
    """Raised when the page cannot be parsed."""

def extract_links(document: str, base_url: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return absolute http(s) links in first-seen order without fragments."""
    if not document.strip():
        raise PageError("empty document")
    tree = html.document_fromstring(document)
    if not isinstance(tree, html.HtmlElement):
        raise PageError("not an HTML document")
    tree.make_links_absolute(base_url, resolve_base_href=True)
    seen: set[str] = set()
    links: list[str] = []
    for element in tree.iter("a"):
        href = element.get("href")
        rel = (element.get("rel") or "").lower().split()
        if not href or "nofollow" in rel:
            continue
        url, _ = urldefrag(href)
        if urlsplit(url).scheme not in ALLOWED_SCHEMES or url in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(url)
        links.append(url)
    return links

candidates.why_wrong: Links are never made absolute, so every relative link is dropped by the scheme filter.
Fragment-only differences produce duplicate URLs for the same page.
Repeated links are returned many times and the crawler refetches them.
Mailto, javascript and ftp URLs are returned as crawlable links.
A NoFollow rel written in mixed case is not recognised and the link is kept.
